Hill-type gene regulatory network

Source: R/model.R
grn.Rd

Builds a network of `n` genes with dynamics $$dx_i/dt = \alpha_i \prod_j H_{ij}(x_j) - \gamma_i x_i,$$ where \(H_{ij}(x) = x^h/(\theta^h + x^h)\) if gene j activates gene i, \(1 - x^h/(\theta^h + x^h)\) if j represses i, and 1 otherwise (with \(\theta = \theta_{ij}\), \(h = h_{ij}\)). The phenotype is the steady state reached by development.

Usage

grn(
  regulation,
  genes = NULL,
  alpha = 1,
  gamma = 1,
  theta = 1,
  hill = 1,
  evolvable = "alpha",
  traits = NULL,
  x0 = 1
)

Arguments

regulation

Either an `n x n` matrix with entries -1, 0 or 1, where `regulation[i, j]` is the effect of gene `j` on gene `i` (+1 activation, -1 repression), or a character vector of edges such as `c("x1 -> x2", "x2 -| x1")`.

genes

Gene names, or the number of genes. Defaults to the row names of `regulation`, or the genes named in the edges (in order of appearance).

alpha, gamma

Production and decay rates (scalar or length `n`). `alpha` values are only defaults when alpha is evolvable.

theta, hill

Regulatory thresholds and Hill coefficients (scalar or `n x n` matrix, indexed like `regulation`).

evolvable

Which parameters are genetically variable loci. Any of `"alpha"`, `"gamma"`, `"theta"`, `"hill"` (all entries of that kind; for theta and hill only existing edges), or single entries such as `"alpha[2]"`, `"theta[2,1]"`, mixed freely.

traits

Genes whose expression is the phenotype under selection (names or indices). Defaults to all genes.

x0

Default initial expression state used when no other starting point is given.

Value

An object of class `hill_grn`.

Examples

# motif 3 of the paper: x2 represses x1, x1 activates x2
m <- grn(c("x1 -> x2", "x2 -| x1"), theta = 5)
# a three-gene repressilator-like cascade with evolvable thresholds
m3 <- grn(c("a -| b", "b -| c", "c -> a"), evolvable = c("alpha", "theta"))
